title: Back-Rank Checkmate
hintText: Look at Black's back rank. Their King is trapped behind their own pawns.

explanation.blunder: Black neglected to push h6 or g6 to give their King a retreat square ('luft').
explanation.takeaway: Always keep an eye on unprotected back ranks. A single major piece can deliver instant mate if the king has no escape.

title: Decisive Overload
hintText: Black has one rook guarding e8. Can you overload or deflect it?

explanation.blunder: Black relied on a single rook on a8 to defend against both the Queen and the Rook.
explanation.takeaway: When a defending piece has more than one obligation, a sacrifice can drag it away, allowing your second attacker to deliver mate.

title: The Royal Knight Fork
hintText: Your knight can jump to a square that attacks both the King and the unprotected rook.

explanation.blunder: Black left the c8-rook unprotected while their King sat on g8 without escape from e7 checks.
explanation.takeaway: Knights are dangerous leapers. Whenever an enemy piece is undefended, calculate if a knight check can simultaneously attack it.

title: Absolute Rook Skewer
hintText: Can you check the King along an open file where the enemy rook is directly behind it?

explanation.blunder: Black lined up their valuable King directly in front of their undefended Rook on the e-file.
explanation.takeaway: A skewer attacks a more valuable piece (the King) that must move, leaving the piece behind it exposed to capture.

title: Morphy's Opera Deflection
hintText: The d7 knight is the only piece stopping Rd8 mate. How do you remove or deflect it?

explanation.blunder: Black left their King stuck in the center without castling, guarded only by the knight on d7.
explanation.takeaway: Paul Morphy demonstrated that time and development trump material. Sacrificing the Queen to remove the defender ends the game immediately.

title: Boden's Mate Theme
hintText: Look at the criss-crossing bishop diagonals towards Black's queenside King.

explanation.blunder: Black's c6 and d7 pawns blocked their own king's flight paths, while two enemy bishops dominated the diagonals.
explanation.takeaway: Pairs of bishops cutting across an open king's position are deadly. Sacrificing a queen on c6 completely breaks open the diagonal for Ba6#.

title: Philidor's Smothered Mate
hintText: Force Black's own rook to surround and trap its King.

explanation.blunder: Black allowed White's knight to control the f7 escape square while the Queen aimed directly at g8.
explanation.takeaway: When an enemy king is hemmed in by its own pawns, sacrifice your queen with check to force their rook to block the king's last exit, setting up a knight mate.

title: Anastasia's Mate
hintText: The knight on e7 walls off g8 and g6. How do you open the h-file for your rook?

explanation.blunder: Black gave up the e7 outpost to White's knight, which created a lethal barrier trapping the King against the board edge.
explanation.takeaway: Knight on e7 + open h-file rook is an unstoppable checkmate pattern. Sacrificing the Queen to pry open the file finishes the combination.
